name: Creating multiple data types together
gist: Papers on generating images paired with other information (text, graphs, molecules, molecular descriptions) or combining different types of input to create richer outputs.
explain: Some generation tasks require creating more than one thing at once. You might want an image paired with a detailed text description, or a molecule paired with predictions of its properties, or a visual diagram paired with the data it represents. The challenge is that different data types have different structure and statistics. An image is a grid of pixels; text is a sequence of words; molecules are graphs where atoms connect to atoms. A single generative model has to somehow handle all these different structures and ensure they're coherent—the image and description have to match, the molecule and its properties have to align.

The core difficulty is coordination. If you generate the image and then try to generate a description, you might get a mismatch. If you try to generate them together, you need a framework that treats both equally. How do you even train a single model on data of such different types? One approach is a shared intermediate representation—convert images, text, and graphs into a common numerical format, let the model work in that format, then convert back. Another is to use multi-modal models (models trained on paired examples of images and text, or text and molecules), which work because the model is repeatedly shown correct pairings and learns to associate certain images with certain kinds of descriptions (a sunset description goes with warm colors, not cool colors). A third is to stack independent models: generate the image, then condition the text-generation model on the image (so the text model can see what was generated and describe it).

Papers here explore these approaches. Some propose new architectures that handle multiple data types naturally. Others work on the training problem—how to learn from paired data of mixed types. Still others focus on specific combinations: text-to-image plus generation of captions, or molecular generation plus property prediction. The motivation is practical: in many real applications, you need multiple outputs that fit together, not just one thing in isolation.

papers.title: FilMaster: Bridging Cinematic Principles and Generative AI for Automated Film Generation
papers.contribution: Generates professional-grade, editable films by learning cinematography from 440,000 real film clips and emulating professional post-production workflows for coherent visual storytelling.

papers.title: ImageRAG: Dynamic Image Retrieval for Reference-Guided Image Generation
papers.contribution: Consistently improves rare and fine-grained concept generation across three datasets and three generative models without requiring RAG-specific training.

papers.title: MoVie: Multimodal Video Compression with Text Guidance
papers.contribution: Achieves -50.23% BD-rate for FID and -14.64% for LPIPS relative to HM while requiring only 55.76% of DCVC-FM's per-pixel computation, with human preference confirmed.

papers.title: RAG4DMC: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Data-Level Modality Completion
papers.contribution: RAG4DMC produces more accurate and semantically coherent missing-modality completions, improving downstream image-text retrieval and image captioning tasks.

papers.title: Unified Multi-Modal Interactive and Reactive 3D Motion Generation via Rectified Flow
papers.contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art performance in two-person multi-modal motion generation with improved quality, responsiveness, and synchronization across interactive and reactive benchmarks.

papers.title: Demystifying Multimodal Biomolecular Co-design With Intrinsic Geodesic Coupling
papers.contribution: Consistently outperforms synchronous and random coupling on structure-based drug design and protein design with improved physical validity.

papers.title: Deterministic Component Mining for Multi-Framework UI2Code Generation
papers.contribution: DCM significantly outperforms baselines on automatic metrics and component-level reuse while maintaining multi-framework portability and code quality.

papers.title: GAGA: Gaussianity-Aware Gaussian Approximation for Efficient 3D Molecular Generation
papers.contribution: GAGA achieves substantial improvement on both generation quality and computational efficiency for 3D molecular generation without sacrificing training granularity.

papers.title: Hölder++: Improving Quality-Coherence Trade-off in Multimodal VAEs
papers.contribution: Hölder++ consistently improves the generative quality-coherence trade-off, yields more structured latent spaces, and learns shared representations useful for downstream tasks.

papers.title: InertialAR: Autoregressive 3D Molecule Generation with Inertial Frames
papers.contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art on 8/10 metrics for unconditional generation; significantly outperforms on controllable generation for targeted chemical functionality.

papers.title: On the Wings of Imagination: Conflicting Script-based Multi-role Framework for Humor Caption Generation
papers.contribution: Outperforms state-of-the-art baselines on two New Yorker Cartoon benchmarking datasets for multi-modal humor captioning.

papers.title: Parallel Multimodal Diffusion Language Models for Thinking-Aware Editing and Generation
papers.contribution: Parallel multimodal diffusion achieves 6.9% improvement in Output Alignment on ParaBench compared to the state-of-the-art model Bagel.

papers.title: PolyGraph Discrepancy: a classifier-based metric for graph generation
papers.contribution: Provides more robust and comparable evaluation metrics across different graph descriptors with theoretically grounded summary scores.

papers.title: Variational Bayesian Flow Network for Graph Generation
papers.contribution: Improves fidelity and diversity on synthetic and molecular graph datasets while surpassing baseline methods through structured precision-based node-edge consistency.

papers.title: VecMol: Vector-Field Representations for 3D Molecule Generation
papers.contribution: Achieves competitive generation quality on QM9 and GEOM-Drugs benchmarks, demonstrating vector-field representation as promising new direction for 3D molecular generation.
